title: Manicouagan Reservoir – The Eye of Quebec

beats.text: Type these coordinates into a satellite map, and you'll find something strange in Quebec's heart.
A perfect circular lake, about seventy kilometers across, rings a massive island.
From space it looks like a giant eye, sometimes called the eye of Quebec.
What could have made such a huge ring so perfectly round?
Scientists say a massive meteor struck here two hundred fourteen million years ago.
The impact crater formed a multi-ring basin, the outer ring about one hundred kilometers wide.
Inside the ring, the island plateau rises nearly a thousand meters, topped by Mount Babel.
That ring is the scar of an ancient collision, not a mystery.
Follow for more places you can see from space.

description: Manicouagan Reservoir is a seventy kilometer diameter annular lake formed by a meteor impact two hundred fourteen million years ago. The crater's outer ring spans about one hundred kilometers and encloses René‑Levasseur Island with Mount Babel rising nearly a thousand meters. Imagery: Esri, Maxar, Earthstar Geographics.
